utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a couple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Further cross-examination by Mr. Weber:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General Masal, I would like to take you back to one of your answers regarding the Strpci abduction. At temporary transcript page 33 of today, you were recorded as saying: "As for this event, I was informed about it when it actually happened." Who did you receive this information from? If you could please just tell us a name. Or names.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, that moment I was not at the command. I was out in the field. My duty officer called me from the operations centre telling me to come back to the command. Within an hour or an hour and a half approximately I was there, and I received this first oral report from the duty officer in my operations centre who just told me, in the briefest possible terms, that that had happened, without giving my any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could just stop there. What is the name of your duty officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedjo Mrsovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who did he receive the information from that he was reporting to you? If you could just give us the name or names.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know by name -- or rather, what he said to me then was that it was the duty officer from another brigade that had called him, the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. The 2nd Brigade. You're referring to the 2nd Podrinje Brigade; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As we've already heard you explain, that's the brigade in Visegrad. What were they doing in Rudo that would have allowed them to know what was going on during the abduction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean that report from the railways? I -- I cannot explain whether anybody from Visegrad was in Rudo. Because obviously they received information from someone that I have no idea about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On page -- --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I don't know if Your Honours have any further questions about that. I was going ask something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions and my colleagues also have no further questions on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At page 36 of today's transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could I ask you: Mr. Ivetic took considerably more than the 35 minutes he indicated. How much more time would you need? If it's a matter of five minutes, then we'll continue and have the break then. If it's more, then we have to consider to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'll be finished by the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On page 36 of today's transcript, you referred to Boban Indjic could only receive orders from his brigade commander. Is it correct you're referring to Luka Dragicevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking about orders, combat orders. He only could receive that from his commander and that is Luka Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have anything else. But since the matter was raised by Jovo Maric and the Drina Corps, the Prosecution has uploaded, although not yet translated, three personnel-related documents at that time related to that individual being assigned to the Drina Corps. They are 65 ter numbers 32322, 32323, 32324. We'd be tendering those documents at this time once translations become available and that will also, I believe, give an opportunity to the Defence to do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no English translations yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the word "pukovnik" appearing somewhere because --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I think that it appears in all three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In all three. Would it not be good then to put that to the witness so that he has an opportunity because his --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's what I was going to suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- evidence now is contradicting apparently the Prosecution's case in this respect, and therefore I think we should give the witness an opportunity to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sure. With the Chamber's indulgence if I -- since I don't have the translations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- I can just call it up and the -- similar information appears in the next two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if we could -- if you would show them to the witness, all three, and then perhaps ask questions. Mr. Masal, the Prosecution will now show you three documents they claim - we haven't seen them yet - that a Jovo Maric was a colonel in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please have a good look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter 32322.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please review this document and let us know when you've completed your review.

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is -- it's correct that this document is to the five brigades that are subordinated to you -- actually, four of the five brigades; the 1st, the 3rd, the 4th, and 5th Podrinje Infantry Brigades?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was sent to these brigades, but I really don't know. I only knew the general, General Jovo Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32323.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we pulled a personnel list related to the Drina Corps from the same month of the document that you're commenting on, February 1993. I think for today's purposes if you could just review the first page, I think even up to the fourth entry, where Jovo Maric appears. You see that; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 32324.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, excuse me. Do you recall -- do you recall that this individual was in fact a part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGISA MASAL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a detail. The single identification normal says that he was born on the 1st of September, 1936. General Jovo Maric was born the same year as I was, in 1951. Obviously this was a pensioner who was activated and who did this kind of work for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you don't have to comment on it. What you testified is that you did not know any Jovo Maric in the Drina Corps apart from knowing a General Jovo Maric, and Mr. Weber puts to you a few documents in which the existence of a Colonel Jovo Maric seems to be documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean, I can keep on going, I'll have a similar question, but we'd just ask to tender the three documents to establish in the record that there was such an individual at the time in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and we see number 3 on our screen at this moment, I think. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But I don't see that name you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the name -- the name --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's in the first line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's in the first line. Yes, something happened apparently on the 7th of August, 1993. No objections, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objections once we get the translations in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, could you assign numbers for those three documents to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 32322 will be MFI P7250. 65 ter number 32323 will be MFI P7251. And 65 ter number 32324 will be MFI P7252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7250, -51, and -52 are marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, this concludes your evidence, but perhaps before I excuse the witness, Mr. Ivetic, the gist of the whole issue of rockets launched from tubes or not from tubes escaped me completely. I do understand that if you launch a rocket not from a tube but if it is attached to an aerial bomb that, of course, the mechanisms are different. But I'm -- I think I missed the gist of what it was all about. Now, I'm not inviting you to explain that in front of the witness. But I just, since the witness will leave us very soon, I -- I wondered whether with one or two questions you should clarify what you actually were demonstrating. If you don't need the witness for that, then we'll excuse the witness and then you may briefly in one or two lines explain what the gist of your questions was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think can I explain without the witness. It relates --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll excuse the witness. Mr. Masal, this concludes your evidence in this court, and I'd like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered all the many questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. You may follow the usher, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic if you can explain in one or two lines, you're invited to do so. Otherwise, we'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With relation to both the questioning by Mr. Groome of Mr. Radojcic and Mr. Weber of this witness, it was suggested that the rockets are not going through the tubes, and the difference between a rifled tube and a non-rifled tube, which I believe Colonel Hamill testified about during the Prosecution case. They're different types of technology and not all artillery is rifled - that is to say, with the grooves that would cause the rotation, and it's not like a gun - and I think the witness explained how the barrel on a multiple-rocket launcher operates and that it is smooth and that's all that I was trying to establish, that the -- there is no rifling for a rocket that is for a shell or for a bullet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't start rotating which stabilises the flight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that what you wanted to establish? Well, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to that explanation, I believe it conflates a number of things and we wouldn't be in accord with that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we don't -- I just wanted to know what it was, not to start any further discussion. But it escaped entirely what I should learn from that. And Mr. Ivetic has now told us that the only thing he wanted to demonstrate, and whether it's relevant in this context is a different matter, of course, and whether it still is relevant if you attach it to an aerial bomb is another matter, but Mr. Ivetic apparently wanted to explain to us that these kind of projectiles are launched in a -- from a barrel or from a tube which is different from most of the artillery tubes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just wanted to clarify and I appreciate what Your Honour is saying. I believe it was the evidence of this witness, and the other witness, that they actually fired along rails, so I believe that -- I just didn't want to get too much confusion about barrels, rails, things like that, and just have that on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that if they are mounted to an aerial bomb that, of course, they are not fired through tubes anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It goes without saying and that's what you're emphasising as well. Rails is then what guides at firing the -- what is sent as a projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I had an entirely non-controversial 30 second matter to address in private session which I can do now or the beginning of next session. Whatever Your Honour prefers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do that after the break, because we have postponed the break already for such a long time. We take a break and resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to enter the courtroom, good afternoon, Mr. Domazet. You appear in order to assist Mr. Blagojevic in -- in relation to his right not to incriminate himself by giving truthful answers. Needless to remind you that, of course, for any fact for which Mr. Blagojevic has already been convicted, he is not at risk to be prosecuted again because the ne bis in idem rule does not allow for such a second prosecution. But of course, there may be matters outside the scope of what he was indicted for and what he was convicted for. But your role is limited to that, nothing else. If that is clear to you, we'll just proceed once the witness has entered the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Blagojevic. Mr. Blagojevic, Mr. Domazet is in this courtroom as well in order to assist you in the context of what we call Rule 90(E), which is that you are not under an obligation to answer any questions if a truthful answer to that question would tend to incriminate yourself. May I take it that you -- that Mr. Domazet explained to you exactly what Rule 90(E) is about?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please come closer to the microphone because the interpreters have difficulties in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I understand that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was explained to you, so I don't have to do that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The back of the seat is too flexible. It should be adjusted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, apart from that, I take it that the Victims and Witness Section has instructed you that you should not greet or seek contact with Mr. Mladic when entering the courtroom. Did they explain that to you? You don't have to look at him; just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been explained to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why, then, did you do it, nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did I do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Seek eye contact, smiled to Mr. Mladic, and receive a similar thing back from him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't take it that way. I looked at everybody else too. I looked at my lawyer as well. I looked at the other lawyers and the others present here. I looked at everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, your focus was on Mr. Mladic, and apart from that, you have not been instructed to look at no one. You have been instructed that you should not seek contact with Mr. Mladic, which you clearly did. All three Judges have observed that and it was the focus of your behaviour at the -- I'm not seeking any further comment from you. You'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll find Mr. Lukic to your left. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For the record, could you please slowly state your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I am Vidoje Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, did you give a statement to the members General Mladic's Defence team?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I gave a statement to the members of the Defence team of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have on our screens, 1D01704.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A document is going to show up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just going to ask for page 3 of this document now, and we'll take a look at paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you drew my attention to something here when we reviewed the documents. You said that it is written the 6th of July. That is what is typed here. And the document that this paragraph refers to says the 5th of July. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This should say "5" instead of "6." It should say the 5th of July, instead of the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're going to take a look at the document later. So this is a correction that we should make in this statement. So paragraph 8 should say "05" instead of "06."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we go back to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, do you see a signature here; and, if so, can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could take a look at the last page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see two signatures here on this page. Can you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: They are my signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After we have corrected the date, is the rest of your statement correct? Has everything been recorded correctly? I'm talking about the entire statement: Is everything correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the correction of the date, and I think that this correction is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the rest of the statement? Has everything been recorded the way you stated things for us?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were -- or, rather, to the best of your knowledge, is everything in the statement truthful?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There will be times when I'm going to pause after your answer before I put a new question to you. This is to give room to the interpreters to interpret your words correctly. I don't want you to be confused by those pauses. If I were to put the same questions to you today, the same ones that we put to you when your statement was taken, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to tender Mr. Blagojevic's statement, 1D017054, into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D965, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D965 is admitted into evidence. If you have any further questions to the witness, Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will just clarify this paragraph 8, and I would kindly ask to have D303 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, what you have before you on the screen is a document dated 5 July 1995. It was issued by the Command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. It is an order for active combat operations, and the operational number is 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After having seen the first page, can we go and look at the last page as well. [In English] We need the bottom of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, at the bottom we see the typed words "Commander, Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic," and we can see a signature. Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is my document. I signed it myself. I compiled it and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this the document referred to in paragraph 8; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the upper left-hand corner you can see the date. I wanted that date to be corrected in the statement, to reflect what is seen in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let's look at the second page. Again, I'm interested in bullet point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the end of that paragraph, we can see that readiness or beginning of the attack is at 0400 hours on the 6th of July, 1995. Does this reflect the situation as it was?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is okay. What we read in bullet point 4 of this decision is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties carefully look at the document again to see whether there are any transcription or translation errors, because in the English version I see "1993." But I take it that everyone would agree that it should be "1995." Now if that's the only thing, I would not send it back to CLSS, but if there are more matters, and I invite the parties to carefully check it, then of course it should be revisited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's already in evidence, but we will check the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I missed it last time, I don't know whether this specific line was addressed when it was admitted --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but at least now it's there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we made this clarification, I would just read summary statement of Mr. Blagojevic, and I will not have more questions for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read the summary of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope the booths have this summary since I distributed it on Thursday. Okay. I can see nodding. Vidoje Blagojevic was a career military officer first in the Yugoslav national army and then in the Army of Republika Srpska. In July 1995, he held the rank of colonel and was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. In response to the frequent excursions of the Muslim forces from the enclave, the Serb political and military leadership made a decision to engage in active combat and reduce the area of the enclave and to separate the enclaves as had been envisaged by the signed agreement, all with the aim of preventing or minimizing the frequent attacks of the Muslim forces from the safe areas of Srebrenica and Zepa. Colonel Blagojevic received and issued orders in early July concerning the Srebrenica combat activities. He never received or gave any order for illegal activities and was not aware of any plan to commit crimes in connection with these combat activities. Colonel Blagojevic was unaware of any plan to execute prisoners from Srebrenica. He states that the claim of Momir Nikolic, that on the evening of 12th of July, 1995, Nikolic informed Colonel Blagojevic of the plan to execute prisoners, is not true. Colonel Blagojevic did not see Momir Nikolic on the evening of 12th of July. During the Srebrenica operation combat activities, nowhere and in no manner did the Bratunac Brigade command provide anyone with any illegal support and assistance that would be aimed against the life of prisoners from the Srebrenica enclave. No such thing was ever ordered or requested from him and the Bratunac Brigade by any of his superiors, nor did he, as the commander, order any such thing to any of his subordinate personnel. And that would be statement summary of Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you'll now be cross-examined by Ms. Hasan. You find Ms. Hasan to your right. And Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution. And I think that still the distance to the microphone and perhaps the position of your chair should be adjusted so that we do not miss a word of your testimony. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I may use my technical knowledge about these chairs, the button that fixes the chair is on the left-hand side. So it cannot be fixed from the right-hand side. No, it's on the left-hand side, the button.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, it's apparently on the other side. We are using all the same chairs, but ... and if you could lean a little bit more forward so that it could be fixed. I see that Mr. Registrar is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You go down with the button.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, and now a bit more closer to the microphone. And then fix it again. No, it's still not okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone being in the right position now, let's get started.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you were found guilty by this Tribunal pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute for aiding and abetting the commission of murder in Bratunac town as a crime against humanity and the violation of laws and customs of war. Do you take responsible for your involvement in that crime?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you straight away: That was an illegal decision of this Tribunal, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. The question was whether you take responsibility for the crimes for which you were convicted. Whether it's legal or not is -- is not asked. Please proceed. And please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether you take responsibility for the crimes for which you were convicted by this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I won't take that responsibility, but I wish to add to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question has been answered. Next question, please, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I take it that your answer that you don't also applies to your conviction under Count 5 for persecution as a crime against humanity through the underlying acts of murder, terrorising civilian population, cruel and inhumane treatment. I take it that applies to that as well. And in addition to that, Count 6, which is inhumane acts as a crime against humanity which was defined as forcible transfer. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Are you right about what?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That you don't take responsibility for those particular crimes as well.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't take responsibility for that either.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, so the record is clear, you were acquitted of your involvement in the overall murder operation. What I would like to turn to now is when you commenced your position as the commander of the Bratunac Brigade in May of 1995, your units were fully under your command, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: My brigade was under my command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you were responsible for -- as a commander for their acts; yes?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: As a commander, I was responsible for being in command over my unit and for controlling its work.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And your responsibility as their commander then, that would include responsibility for acts including crimes committed by those units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My command and control covered the entire work of my unit; of my brigade, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that you were also responsible for prisoners who were detained within your zone of responsibility and who were guarded by your -- members of your units?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to ask you what prisoners and what do you mean "your zone of responsibility"? Please be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm asking you a more general question at this point. If there are prisoners within the Bratunac area of responsibility, okay? Do you take responsibility for those prisoners detained there?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- probably slip of the tongue. It says Bratunac area of responsibility. Maybe you -- my learned friend wanted to ask Bratunac Brigade area of responsibility or what, but there is no Bratunac area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there is a Bratunac area but that's not a very precise description. Ms. Hasan, would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So my question relates to the Bratunac area of -- Bratunac Brigade area of responsibility and specifically whether you take responsibility for prisoners who are detained in that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, we have to intervene here. Maybe we should define first what is zone of responsibility of Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think zone of responsibility is usually is a -- is a general description. And since we, at this moment, are still exploring the general rule and not yet details because, Ms. Hasan, what the witness says could you tell us what prisoners, you said I am asking just in general terms. For that reason at this moment we do not need to clarify it, but perhaps later on we'll have to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And Mr. Lukic, Ms. Hasan used the term "area of responsibility" and not "zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it should be clarified with this gentleman what he considers his area and what is by the rules his area of responsibility. First, to be able to see if there is anybody placed by the -- or anybody from the prisoner group was placed at that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we at this moment are not talking about a specific group or any, or I would say, live prisoners. It's just a question at this moment on the more or less general theoretical level, whether Mr. Blagojevic would be responsible for any prisoners if there were any within the zone of responsibility of the unit he commanded. That's the question, Ms. Hasan, if I understood you well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, you have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the witness please answer that question. If you want to have it repeated, I'll invite Ms. Hasan to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to hear a very concrete question, irrespective of the fact whether it's practical -- of a practical nature or of a theoretical nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Ms. Hasan who formulates the questions. And if you would like to hear another question, it's a pity for you, but you have to answer the question as put to you. Do you want Ms. Hasan to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let her repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, in your area of responsibility, and you know your area of responsibility, if there are prisoners within that area, any part of that area, any prisoners, are you responsible for those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I must say in very precise military terms that I had the zone of defence of the Bratunac Brigade at the relevant time. I'm not going to try and define the zone of defence of the Bratunac Brigade. If somebody wants me to, I will. In any case, I didn't have any prisoners in the zone of defence of the Bratunac Brigade, and if I had had them, I would have been responsible for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you became commander of the Bratunac Brigade on the 25th of May, 1995; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I assumed my official duties on the 25th of May, 1995, and became the commander of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we briefly look at 65 ter 04202.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This -- what you'll see here, it's a document you've seen before, Mr. Blagojevic, and it's a regular combat report. It's from the 25th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we could just briefly, in the B/C/S, turn to page 3 where we see the handwritten version of this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, you recognise your signature on the bottom of that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can just scroll down a little bit so that we can see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see this now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And under item 2, it provides that you took over command at 10.00 in the morning. Do you see that? 1000 hours.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And that's accurate?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to the document and according to what I remember, this is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just at the beginning of the document, under item 1, it reads: "The enemy did not conduct combat operations against our forces." It continues in the first line of item 2: "Our forces did not open fire towards the demilitarised zone." Now this is a report, and it's from 16 -- so 4.00 p.m. Do you see -- at the bottom there, we see a handwritten notation.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's somewhere else. Maybe on a different page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we go back to the -- page 1 of the B/C/S document where we can see the handwritten notation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, had there been such firing into the demilitarised zone, it's something that you -- that would have required orders from you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say here? I can't see that fire was opened.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let me just restate my question. It says here that your forces did not fire -- did not open fire towards the demilitarised zone. And my question is: Had your forces opened fire, it would have been something you would have been made aware of and in fact you would have ordered; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: If my subordinated units had to open fire on Srebrenica enclave, there would have had to be a reason for that. So if fire had come from the enclave, I'm sure that I would have issued an order to respond with firing at the locations from which fire had been opened in the first place. That's how I would have reacted, and that's the kind of order I would have issued to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we now take a look at 65 ter 06034, please. Oh, and I'd offer 65 ter 04202 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7253, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now we see here, this is a very urgent order. It bears strictly confidential number 08/8-60. We can just keep that in mind because I'll get back to that. And it's an order from General Zivanovic. It's informing all units that -- we can see here in the second -- in the first main paragraph, that: "At 1558 hours the forces of the NATO Pact have carried out a fire attack against the Jahorinski Potok warehouse ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that at the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This was a weapons warehouse near Pale; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. I suppose that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And General Zivanovic orders under item 1 in relation to that, that the Drina Corps forces are to remain in full combat readiness, and he orders the raising of combat readiness to the highest level and specifies that any opening of fire shall be regulated by the Drina Corps through the Grabovica signals table. Now, we see at the top that this order is addressed to a number of brigades, including the Bratunac Brigade; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So this is an order you received; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that it arrived in the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 06034 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7254, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now this would have been an order would you have -- you received on the -- this is still -- we're talking here about your first day at work, isn't that right, as a brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that I received it on that day that we are talking about, the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether, on the -- whether the 25th of May, which is the date of this order, was the first day you were in office as commander of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: 25th of May, 1995, was the first day when I assumed my duty and started commanding the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And not long after NATO attacked the weapons warehouse, you ordered your units to fire at the inhabited Srebrenica enclave, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know on the basis of what you are saying that. I'm saying that that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter 06025, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, while waiting for that document, may I draw your attention to the fact that earlier you -- in one question you dealt with receiving an order on the same date as taking up duties. And that you said, "I asked you," and then you phrased as question which covered only one part of your question. I don't know whether you're interested in whether or not the witness received it or not, but he until now only testified that the unit received it. Perhaps you'll re-read it later. There's no need to immediately deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if we take a look at this interim combat report, it's dated 25 May 1995 from the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and we see your name there at the bottom and an indication there in handwritten note that it's delivered at 2110 hours on 25 May; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now this goes to the Drina Corps, and at paragraph 3, it reads: "We have taken steps in accordance with your order strictly confidential number 08/8-60 of 25 May 1995." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this confidential number, if you recall, is just the document we looked at, General Zivanovic's order. Does that confirm to you whether or not your command received that order on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: This sentence that you read out to me confirms some other measures that were contained in the previous document, and they include those measures too. You read out just part of that document. You didn't read it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But we can agree that it means that the order we just looked at from General Zivanovic was received by your brigade command on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms that consistently.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we look at item 1, this report provides that: "In accordance with an oral order from Colonel Lazic, we fired two shells from 105-millimetre howitzers (a total of four shells) on the town of Srebrenica at 1907 hours." It goes on to provide that: "Artillery observers at Pribicevac reported that two shells fell near the Domavija feature. The other two shells were not observed but they fell on Srebrenica." Now the Domavija is -- feature, that's the hotel in the Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Conditionally speaking, yes, it's a hotel, but at that time it wasn't used for those purposes. It was used for military purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the other two shells, as indicated here, the artillery observers at Pribicevac, they did not see -- they did not see those shells, did they, as is reported here?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you take responsibility for firing those shells?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, this -- if I can take you, actually, back to -- actually, I won't go there yet, but I'll ask you this now: Colonel Lazic here is recorded as having issued an oral order, "and in accordance with that, we, the Bratunac Brigade, fired the two shells." Now isn't it correct, Mr. Blagojevic, that you would be -- you would have been the commander who implemented Colonel Lazic's order?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that Colonel Lazic issued the order orally. It wasn't issued on paper. He issued it orally. But he issued it to the crew who were doing the firing and he had communication with the artillery observers who showed the targets that were supposed to be engaged.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you remind us who Colonel Lazic is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we're talking about the same person, Colonel Lazic - Milan, I think, his first name was, if I'm not mistaken - he was from the corps command, from the operations organ, as far as I can remember, so that was my immediate superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Blagojevic, you recall testifying in the Karadzic case, don't you? This was in December of 2013.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a witness in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you tell the truth in that case?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I'm telling the truth now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we just briefly then look at Mr. Blagojevic's Karadzic testimony, which is 65 ter 32300. And if we could look at page 40, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you were asked in that case at line 8: "Q. So do you take responsibility for firing these howitzers shells on the Srebrenica enclave? "A. Partly, yes. "Q. What do you mean "partly"? "A. Because of the oral order I received from Colonel Lazic. He was there. It's in the report. You have read it out. He represented the superior command. "Q. Yes. He shares responsibility from the Drina Corps, as did anyone that may have issued orders from the Main Staff, as is anyone from the Presidency that may have also have issued such an order; correct. "A. It's not about sharing. It's about assuming responsibility. He assumes responsibility because he was there and he issued that order to me." So, Mr. Blagojevic, do you stand by that testimony you gave.

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Now? I stand by what I said previously in the Karadzic case and what I said today. I can't see any difference. I said all the same things.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you assume responsibility for your units firing these shells?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot assume it because I was not the initiator of this activity. That activity was initiated from a command that was my superior command, and the protagonist was there and he carried that out. It is a fact that artillery pieces were from the Bratunac Brigade but that does not resolve anything in particular because it was military principles that were being abided by. The superior command did that and noticed military targets were engaged, artillery observers indicated that, and that is what it has to do with to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sir, you said in the Karadzic case that you had received the order from Colonel Lazic. We -- I've just read that out. So you received this order from Colonel Lazic. Your units implement this order. Are you saying your units are responsible and you are not?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. It's not the way you are presenting it. Colonel Lazic went to the artillery position, he communicated with the observers, and he carried this operation out. That is the situation. Not the way you've been putting it, that he issued an order to me, and that he --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please start his answer again. It was too fast for precise interpretation of each and every word. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Could you please re-start your answer because you are speaking too quickly for the interpreters to interpret all of your words. Could you please restart your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I said. Colonel Lazic, and we have already said that he's from the operations organ of the Drina Corps, he was at the firing position of that artillery unit. He established communication with the artillery observers who gave him the targets. He issued the order to have these artillery pieces fire, and that was it. That is how this situation evolved. My role, I was not there directly. I know through all of this, I know through this report about all of this. I know about how this -- about what this report says, but I did not take part in what actually evolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you testified in accordance with the truth in Karadzic and you testified today truthfully as well. There are two clear differences: The one is in Karadzic you said that you partially take responsibility; whereas, today you said you take no responsibility. The second is that in the Karadzic case you told that Lazic had issued the order to you; whereas, today you've told us that Lazic did issue the order directly to the crew. These are two differences in two matters. Just for you to know that it's difficult to reconcile you telling us that you testified truthfully both in Karadzic and here where there are these differences. Ms. Hasan, we don't have to spend ages on it. The matter seems to be clear. But if you have in the further comment on this, please give it. Otherwise, Ms. Hasan will put her next question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In addition do that, if we could look ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto even found another difference which he may explain to you. But first would you explain on the differences I already pointed at? If you want to do that. If you don't have further explanations, then perhaps the third one will be put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In addition to that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. I do. I do wish to say something. Because I'm speaking on the basis of facts. To my best recollection. And since you insist, I will try to say why I said this, partly. It can only pertain to the following; namely, that these artillery pieces were within the Bratunac Brigade or rather the property of the Bratunac Brigade. Well, that would be that, what I would like to say by way of an additional point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have just told us a few minutes ago that Mr. Lazic gave the order and you were not there when the order was undertaken. In your report to the Drina Corps, which we saw a few minutes ago, you said "we launched a firing" into Srebrenica. Now, you didn't say, "My units did so on Lazic's orders." You said, "We did." That's another difference that I just want to point out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond? May I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to point out a difference to you. You can decide whether you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to respond. I wish to give you an answer. This is a daily combat report that we are speaking about and it is compiled at the brigade command. It is written by an organ, by a part of the brigade, by a person from the brigade. He formulated it in this way. It is formulated briefly, anyway. And clearly because it's sent by this -- this -- I mean, stenography, and that's the way it is. Perhaps at that moment I did not pay attention to it. It wasn't the way I would have wanted it to be. But what is written there is written, and I have told you everything else on the basis of the facts that I recall in good faith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, let me just put one clarification question. You said Colonel Lazic issued this order. Can you tell me to whom this order was issued orally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the crew. The unit. The artillery unit that is operating the artillery piece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you said a minute ago that you were not present. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he issued those orders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I wasn't present. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But again, why did you say in the Karadzic case, that is line 12 in front of us: "Because of the oral order I received from Colonel Lazic ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what's written in the transcript, but that doesn't change things significantly. I am just telling you how this was carried out on the basis of facts. Now, you can compare that to my statement and you can see where the truth lies. And the truth is there in the answer that I provided, in what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And some lines further down you said in the Karadzic case: "He assumes responsibility because he was there and he issued that order to me." That is what you said in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm saying that now too. That he assumes responsibility for the implementation of that military activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes. But you said he issued the order to you. That is what you said. Twice in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how it was interpreted or how it was written down, but I said the same thing. I said the same thing that I'm telling you right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as it is recorded it's not exactly the same. If you challenge the accuracy of what you said, the transcript, or if you challenge the interpretation of your words, we have an opportunity to check that. If that's what you want, then we'll do it. And, Mr. Lukic, I don't know whether you have paid any attention to the words of this witness in the Karadzic case in the original version, that is, the B/C/S he spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to admit that I read the transcript in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In English, okay. Then if the witness insists -- if you insist that's not what you said, then we'll verify it. If you say it's possible that that's what I said, then we leave it as it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no doubt as to what I've been saying. I'm telling the truth. I'm speaking to the best of my recollection, and you can check and verify whatever you wish. That is for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's important for you as well because it may be relevant for the assessment of the reliability and the credibility of your evidence, but in all fairness to the accused we'll have it verified. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just a quick question. I note that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's even beyond the time. We'll take a break. Witness, you may follow the usher. We'll resume at ten minutes to -- no, not -- at five minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Before we take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, we are now entering in the next break. It may be clear that you should not speak with the witness about his testimony in any way. You can talk about the weather if you wish but nothing else. And, of course, if you would not meet, then, of course, even any appearance of this happening would be -- would not even come to anyone's mind, but the instruction simply is that if you speak to the witness, no -- the -- the testimony of the witness, whether already given or still to be given should not be the subject of your conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, I had no intention to speak with the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we take a break and will resume at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I'd briefly like to address to short matter. I think I earlier said when I addressed you, page 72, I said: "I don't know whether you're interested in whether or not the witness received it or not, but he until now only testified that the unit received it." I think that even that's not what he testified, that the -- I just want to correct myself, that -- and then there's no need to follow it up, because I think you addressed the matter, but I just want to correct myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just one quick matter relating to Mr. Blagojevic. I understand from his counsel that he has been explained the Rule 90(E) caution. It's been explained to him. However, I'll leave it your hands whether it, in fact, is appropriate to give to him nonetheless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think that he is assisted by counsel, he has discussed matter with counsel, so therefore I think that the Chamber doesn't need to further intervene. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I did come up with a way to avoid going into private session, which wouldn't have been useful in this context anyway, and that was to indicate to the Court that with respect to the motion that was filed confidentially on March 13th, it was the only one, we have no objection. So if -- I hope that's not too cryptic. If it is, we can revisit it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll carefully check -- how many motions were filed on the 13th of March?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Only one. He said it's the only one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But thank you for the information, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could I offer 65 ter 06025 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which, again, was ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The interim combat report we were looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7255, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we now have 06024, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, this is a report from artillery -- Bratunac Brigade artillery chief, Captain Mico Gavric. It's to the Drina Corps Command. And he writes: "At 1907 hour, we opened fire on Srebrenica on Colonel Lazic's order [sic]. As the first missile was being fired from the 105-millimetre howitzer number 1120, the recoil was greater than usual and the back section became stuck in the back position." And he goes on to say it's necessary to fix that. Now, Mr. Blagojevic, Mr. Gavric here is reporting about on the firing on Srebrenica, and either he was authorised to do so by Colonel Lazic directly on the orders of the Drina Corps, or Colonel Lazic went through you, which is what you had stated in the Karadzic case. So which one of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: First of all, let me tell you what Mr. Gavric's role was. Gavric was the chief of artillery. At the same time, he was the commander of that unit. From all we can see here, he was there when this activity was carried out on the order of Mr. Lazic. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. But my question is: Did you authorise Lazic to directly order Captain Gavric, or was Lazic going through you and you ordered Gavric to fire? Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't order Gavric to open fire. He was in contact with Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now I apologise, Your Honours, because we -- this is not going to appear on the screen. It's an excerpt from the Popovic case of Mr. Gavric's testimony. And I'd like to read what he says out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And why is it not on our screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Because the matter just arose now and it hasn't -- it's not uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then please -- well, if you read it slowly and I take it that the Defence will have an opportunity to further -- if you give the source of it, that means day, case, et cetera, page numbers, then we'll proceed on that basis, and if could you upload the relevant portion as well, not necessarily for admission but just to give access to the Defence to that portion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's transcript pages 26539, and it begins at line 11, and it goes through to transcript page 26540. And again this is from Mico Gavric's Popovic testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the date of the testimony was? Because that often is the clue to finding the relevant transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: 1st October 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The question posed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And up to what line in the next page?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Line 3, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The question posed is: "Now you testified that Colonel Lazic arrived with his order. What did he tell you about the order? And I understand now you are telling us it's an oral order; right? "A. You are asking me about something and can I only tell you this. My commander was there. I didn't talk with Colonel Lazic. It was Colonel Blagojevic that was in a position to talk to Colonel Lazic, not myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Stewart tells me that she can display it on Sanction for everyone to follow along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If she would do that, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So there it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If I continue, line 18: "Q. Colonel Blagojevic was in command at this time, what was his position in May 1995, May 25th? "A. It so happened that he was there on that day. "Q. In what capacity? "A. He was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. "Q. And what discussion did you have with Colonel Blagojevic about the need to secure authorisation from a higher command to fire on the safe area in violation of the law? "A. I did not discuss that with him. If a report arrived, the brigade commander was put in the picture and that's all ... I can tell you."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, do you dispute what Mr. Gavric said here under oath?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Why should I dispute him? I wouldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And now the firing crew that fired on Srebrenica, they're responsible for their actions; is that right? You'd agree, that your units who fired are responsible?

utterances.speaker: VIDOJE BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are responsible for their own actions and what they did with the equipment that they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer 65 ter 06024 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it after it's uploaded? Is that ... or is it uploaded? Let me just check. I'm always -- oh, it's the previous document I do understand and not the transcript. Mr. Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7256, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Ms. Hasan, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see we're out of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Blagojevic, we'll adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.30 in this same courtroom. But before you leave this courtroom, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given or it's testimony still to be given, and that includes any conversation you may have with Mr. Domazet. So no discussions about your testimony either given or still to be given. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 24th of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
